scenario: AITA for telling my mom she was a bad mother? | So this is kind of a two part thing. A while back, I made my mother upset because of a couple different things I said while out with her. She was saying something about how she didn't believe in doctors and that my siblings literally beg her to go and she still puts off taking them as long as possible. I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. She didn't take that too well, but ended up dropping it and brushing it off as no big deal. Later on, she asked me to go grab her a drink and when I asked her what she wanted she said "well you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" And I told her no, I do not know what you like, my grandparents raised me, I still don't know anything about you. She got upset and started crying and said "what's your problem!? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean I was just saying it's not cool to not take your kid to the doctor and that I'm not going to know anything about her since I didnt grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (that a different family member pays for) and I wanted him to have his own, so I made it clear they can keep his other one and this one is STRICTLY for him. Well I found out they've been taking and using this one too, so when I saw her I told her, seriously, I dont want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him. That is HIS that I'M paying for, not you, it is not yours to touch, it's already bad enough that you keep all his work money at least don't touch his phone. She got upset and starting yelling and crying saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well to be honest she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown and started sobbing and said well fine, I don't need you in my life anyways, and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

First, the background: The person had some serious health issues as a child because their mom didn't take them to the doctor, which almost led to their death. They were hospitalized for weeks and had to recover on bedrest for months. That's a really traumatic experience. So, when the mom made comments about not believing in doctors and putting off taking the siblings to the doctor, the person understandably got upset and confronted her about it. They told her that her actions were not okay and could lead to someone dying. That's a strong statement, but given the past experience, it's understandable why they felt the need to speak up. Then, later, the mom asked the person to get her a drink and made a comment about having raised them for 26 years, implying they should know her preferences. The person responded by saying they didn't know her because they were raised by their grandparents. This led to the mom feeling upset and crying, accusing the person of being mean and trying to make her seem bad. The person defended themselves by saying they weren't trying to be mean but were just pointing out that not taking kids to the doctor isn't cool and that they don't know her because they didn't grow up with her. A few weeks later, they went out again. The person had bought their brother a phone because the family kept taking his other phone, which was paid for by a different family member. They made it clear that this new phone was strictly for the brother. However, they found out that the family was still taking and using the new phone. When they confronted their mom about this, they told her they didn't want to take the phone back because they didn't want the brother to be punished, but they would if the mom didn't stop stealing it. They also mentioned that the mom was keeping all the brother's work money, which added to the frustration. The mom got upset, started yelling and crying, and accused the person of treating her like a bad mother. The person then told her that, honestly, she kind of is one. The mom had a meltdown, said she didn't need the person in her life, and left. Now, the family is saying the person shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't great to them. The question is whether the person did the right thing (AITA - Am I the Asshole?). So, thinking about this, the person has had a lot of valid reasons to be upset with their mom. The mom's refusal to take them to the doctor led to a near-death experience, which is a serious issue. Confronting her about that seems justified because it's a matter of life and death. However, the way they confronted her might have been harsh, but given the circumstances, it's understandable. In the second instance, the mom's comment about having raised them for 26 years was insensitive because the person was actually raised by their grandparents. That must have been hurtful, and the person's response was a way to set boundaries and express their feelings. It's important to communicate feelings, but the way it was done might have been too direct, leading to the mom feeling attacked. The third situation involves the phone. The person was trying to help their brother by providing him with his own phone, but the mom was taking it and using it. The person was trying to protect their brother from being punished for the mom's actions, which is kind. However, confronting the mom in that moment, especially after the previous incidents, might have been the tipping point. Telling the mom she's a bad mother was a strong statement, and while it's based on past experiences, it's a harsh way to express it. The family's reaction is that the person shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't great. This suggests that they value the relationship with the mom more than addressing the issues, or perhaps they think that confronting her in that way was unnecessary or unkind. On one hand, the person has every right to express their feelings and set boundaries, especially regarding their health and their brother's well-being. On the other hand, the way they expressed it might have been too confrontational, leading to the breakdown of the relationship. I think it's a tough situation because the person has valid grievances, but the method of addressing them might have been too harsh. It's important to communicate feelings, but doing so in a way that's constructive rather than confrontational can be more effective. However, given the mom's past behavior and the person's trauma, it's understandable why they might have lost their patience. In conclusion, while the person's feelings are valid, the way they expressed them might have been too harsh, leading to the mom feeling attacked. Therefore, they might be the asshole in this situation because the method of confrontation could have been handled more diplomatically, even if the underlying issues are legitimate.
